title: Stewardship Traffic Orchestra and A/B Pulse Playbook (working)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight operational playbook for cross-functional stewards to run short-cycle A/B experiments and staged canaries across heterogeneous inference routes. Focus is on rapid detection, human-in-loop stabilization, and safe reversion paths when models or routing changes degrade quality, latency, or cost metrics.

Context/why this exists:
- Many teams run canaries in isolation; we end up with inconsistent guardrails and slow response when multiple experiments interact.
- We need a shared choreography for: steward roles, telemetry thresholds, traffic choreography (burst vs steady), and quick rollback workflows.

Quick glossary (team vernacular):
- Steward: person responsible for observing a release window and executing fallbacks.
- Orchestra: the set of traffic routing knobs + human actions used to shepherd exposure (weights, slices, traffic priming, synthetic injections).
- Pulse: a short-period telemetry check (5m, 30m, 6h) used to decide proceed/pause/rewind.
- Drift event: sudden degradation in quality signals (LLM hallucination rate, moderation flags, NPS) or SLO breach.

Pre-launch checklist (owner: release lead, confirm with stewards):
- Define hypothesis: expected delta (e.g., +3% conversion, <=5ms p50 latency change).
- Traffic slices: identify at least 3 independent slices (control, slice-A, slice-B) and a synthetic probe population (internal test users).
- Telemetry bundle: list of signals and owners (latency p50/p95, token-cost, hard-fail rates, semantic-quality samples, moderation count).
- Minimum dataset for rollback: set of sample prompts + baseline outputs and grading rubric.
- Blast radius cap: maximum % of total traffic and regional limits.
- Activation window: start time, keep window <= 4 hours for first micro-exposure.
- Oncall pager: who is primary/backup and SLAs for acknowledgement (10m) and action (30m).

Steward roles and responsibilities:
- Primary Steward (observability): monitor dashboards, run post-exposure quick checks, escalate.
- Traffic Conductor (ops): apply traffic weights, execute throttles/balancing, coordinate with infra for scale.
- Quality Lead (product/ML): spot-check outputs, maintain sample rubric, call for soft-fail or rollback.
- Comms Lead: update stakeholders, customer success, legal if necessary.
- Reserve: person to author the rollback CR and own the IR afterwards.

Activation cadence (recommended defaults):
1) Warmup (0 -> 0.5% over 10m): small synthetic probes + internal cohorts.
2) Micro-exposure (0.5% -> 3% over 30m): start Pulse checks every 5m for first 30m.
3) Observe (3% steady for 1h): run 30m and 1h pulses, manual sample review.
4) Expand (3% -> 10% over next 2h) if pulses green.
5) Hold and evaluate with longer fidelity metrics (6h pulse) before moving to staged ramp.

Pulse definitions and thresholds (examples):
- Safety pulse (5m): any hard-fail or error spike > 0.5% => immediate traffic revert to last stable route.
- Latency pulse (5m): p95 increase > 40% or absolute p95 > 1200ms for route => scale-back traffic by 50% and open infra ticket.
- Cost pulse (30m): token cost per request increase > 30% => reduced weight and finance notified.
- Quality pulse (30m, manual + automatic): semantic regret score drop > 5 points (relative) or moderation flags > 2x baseline => pause rollout and urgent review.

Signal instrumentation notes:
- Maintain a single source-of-truth dashboard per experiment with the following tabs: routing weights, synthetic probe health, per-slice quality sampling, error logs, kv-cache hit rates.
- Tag logs with experiment id and steward id to filter quickly.
- Export sampled requests/outputs to a temporary evaluation store (48–72h retention) for manual review.

Operational patterns and heuristics:
- If two experiments touch same model family or cache namespace, treat as coupled and reduce combined exposure by 50%.
- Prefer vertical slices (user cohorts) for A/B when behavior-dependent (personalization) and horizontal sampling for infrastructure/routing tests.
- For rerankers and small-output models, prefer larger micro-exposure (>=5%) because signal variance is low.

Rollback decision matrix (fast path):
- Auto-rollback if safety pulse triggers (see thresholds).
- Manual rollback if two of three quality signals degrade: manual review by Quality Lead required within 60m.
- Soft-fallback option: route only failing requests to control variant and keep rest on canary (used when degradation is localized to slice).

Postmortem and retro checklist (if rollback or incident):
- Preserve evaluation store snapshot + raw logs (do not delete).
- Timeline: collect steward logs, chat transcripts, infra events.
- RCA owner assignment within 48 hours.
- Action items: tagging owner, due date, and linking to Jira.

Quick runbook snippets (copyable):
- Set traffic weight: curl -X POST /api/route-weight -d '{"experiment_id":"EXP-2025-11-04","weight":0.03}'
- Trigger synthetic probe burst: /internal/probe?experiment=EXP-2025-11-04&type=priming&count=100
- Snapshot sample store: /admin/eval/snapshot?exp=EXP-2025-11-04&retain=72h

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we adopt a unified semantic-regret metric for cross-team quality comparisons? (Quality leads to decide)
- Do we standardize pulse durations (e.g., 5m/30m/6h) across org or allow product teams to tune?
- Investigate automated partial-fallback routing for partial-degradation cases (route-by-intent).

Appendix: quick templates
- Pre-launch note (Slack): "Starting micro-exposure EXP-2025-11-04 at 11:10 PST. Primary steward: Lena Kim (pager). Observe pulses 5m/30m/1h. Rollback criteria posted in thread."
- Post-exposure summary bullets: hypothesis, max exposure reached, signals (green/yellow/red), action taken, next steps, ticket links.

Related artifacts and readings:
- confluence://rollouts/activation-patterns-2025
- JIRA INF-876 (traffic-conductor improvements backlog)
- repo: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sim (traffic scheduler docs)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc deliberately lean; big playbooks get ignored. Real value is the steward checklist and the pulse definitions.
- Run a practice rehearsal before handing to non-ops PMs. Use simulated traffic for at least one micro-exposure.
